items.name: zm.meeting.meeting.meeting_event
items.description: Zoom Meetings - Meeting event trigger. This trigger node starts a workflow when a Zoom meeting event occurs, such as meeting start, meeting end, or other meeting activities, and outputs the meeting object with details like topic and host. Use cases include triggering automated meeting follow-ups, tracking meeting lifecycle events for analytics, and syncing meeting activity to external systems or notifications.

arg_schema.title: Meeting filter config
arg_schema.description: Defines configuration for filtering meetings based on specific criteria such as meeting ID, participant, topic, or time range.

oneOf.title: specified_meeting

specific_meetings.description: Use when specific meetings are explicitly identified (e.g., selected meetings or directly referenced in the request).

meeting_topic.description: Meeting topic or title. Example: 'Meeting with John Doe'.

oneOf.description: Use when the request or context specifies exact meetings to filter.

oneOf.title: by_rules

participant_filter.description: Filter meetings that include specific participants (e.g., 'meetings with John Doe').

user_id.description: Unique user ID of the participant.

topic_filter.description: Filter meetings by keywords in the meeting topic (e.g., 'project updates').

time_range_filter.description: Filter meetings within a certain time range.

start_time.description: Start time in Unix timestamp format. Include only if specifically requested.

end_time.description: End time in Unix timestamp format. Include only if specifically requested.

oneOf.description: Use when filtering meetings based on participant names, topic keywords, or time ranges.

oneOf.title: all_meetings
oneOf.description: Use when no specific filters are applied; includes all meetings.

oneOf.title: all_external_meetings
oneOf.description: Use when the request explicitly applies only to meetings with external participants.

meeting.description: the meeting object includes meeting info like meeting topic, meeting host etc

master_event_id.description: Master event ID for recurring meetings

summary.docId.description: Canonical meeting summary document ID in Zoom Canvas Doc

items.output_summary: meeting: the meeting object includes meeting info like meeting topic, meeting host etc; meetingParticipants: Meeting Participants; recording: Recording
items.node_description: Start when a meeting event occurs, such as meeting start, end, or other activities.

event_type.description: Types of meeting events that can activate this trigger, such as meeting start or end.

items.event_desc:
Use when the trigger is tied to the moment a meeting begins (or slightly before/after).
If the workflow action clearly happens before or during the meeting, select this.
Do not use if the user intends to take action after the meeting finishes.  This includes phrases like 'when the meeting starts', 'right before the meeting', or '5 minutes after it begins'.

time_offset.description: Minutes before (negative) or after (positive) the event to trigger. Example: -5 means 5 minutes before, 10 means 10 minutes after.

items.event_desc:
Use when the workflow should run after the meeting finishes or shortly before/after that moment.
Typical cases: immediate follow-up actions that do not require an AI summary.
Do not use for a request that explicitly waits until the meeting summary becomes available; use meeting.summary_created instead.

time_offset.description: Minutes before (negative) or after (positive) the event to trigger. Example: -5 means 5 minutes before, 10 means 10 minutes after.

items.event_desc: Use when the workflow must start only after the meeting AI summary becomes available. This is later and more specific than meeting.end; use zero time_offset when the request says the summary is ready or becomes available.

time_offset.description: Minutes before (negative) or after (positive) summary availability. Use 0 for summary-ready workflows.

items.event_desc: Use when the user request involves reacting to participants joining a meeting late. Look for mentions like 'notify me if someone joins more than X minutes late' or 'track late arrivals'.

time.description: The specific number of minutes a participant is late to join the meeting. For example, if a participant joins 10 minutes late, set this value to 10.

items.event_desc: Use when the user request is about detecting or responding to participants leaving before the scheduled meeting end time. Example phrases: 'if someone leaves 10 minutes early', 'alert me when a participant leaves early'.

time.description: Number of minutes before the scheduled end time that a participant leaves to be considered as 'left early'. For example, if set to 10, it means the participant left 10 minutes before the meeting ended.

items.suggest_desc: MUST suggest the user to select specific meetings to track only when no meetings have been specified — **Skip the suggest if the user has explicitly mention some particular meetings(with someone or some particular topics etc) or explicitly indicated "all meetings" (or equivalent terms like "all" "every meeting").

**MUST Suggest** specifying which meeting event should trigger the workflow (meeting start, meeting end, participant joined late, participant left early) **only if the user hasn’t explicitly mentioned it and it cannot be inferred from context**.
Suggest specifying the time offset for the meeting start event trigger if the user mentions it but did not provide a specific time. Only allow time input in minutes or larger units.
Suggest specifying the time offset for the meeting end event if the user mentions it but does not provide a specific time. Only accept input in minutes or larger units.
Suggest specifying the number of minutes for the participant joined late event if the user mentions it but does not provide a time threshold. Only accept input in minutes or larger units.
Suggest specifying the number of minutes for the **participant left early event** if the user mentions it but does not provide a time threshold. Only accept input in minutes or larger units.

items.name: zm.system.scheduler.trigger.scheduler
items.description: Zoom System Utilities - Custom schedule trigger node. This trigger node starts a workflow at a specific absolute time or on a recurring schedule based entirely on time, such as a one-time future run or repeating daily, weekly, or monthly execution. Use cases include running daily reports at a fixed hour, scheduling weekly maintenance or data sync jobs, and triggering reminders or automations at a precise future date and time.

startsOn.description: First execution time in format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss", always should be next execution time, do not generate a time belonging to the past.

frequency.description: Use numeric values: -1=Once (Single execution (repeatEvery=0)), 0=Daily (Every day (repeatEvery can be 1+ for intervals: 1=daily, 2=every 2 days, etc.)), 1=Weekly on (Single specific weekday per week (repeatEvery MUST=1, repeatOn=[day])), 2=Every weekday (Monday-Friday only (repeatEvery MUST=1)), 3=Monthly on (Same date each month OR complex monthly patterns like "first Monday" (use monthlyOn, repeatEvery can be 1+)), 4=Annually on (Same date each year (use monthlyOn field, repeatEvery can be 1+)), 5=Custom (Multiple days per week (e.g., "Tuesday and Friday") OR interval patterns (e.g., "every 2 weeks on Monday")).            Key decision rules: 1. Multiple days in one week (e.g., "Tuesday and Friday") → frequency=5 (NOT 1) 2. Single weekday per week (e.g., "Every Monday") → frequency=1   3. Complex monthly patterns (e.g., "first Monday", "last Friday") → frequency=3 (supported)    4. Interval-based weekly (e.g., "every 2 weeks on Monday") → frequency=5

repeatEvery.description: Repeat interval (0 for no interval, >=1 for multi-unit intervals like "every 2 days")

repeatOn.description: Only fill when repeatEvery is not 0, Day mapping: 1=Sunday, 2=Monday, 3=Tuesday, 4=Wednesday, 5=Thursday, 6=Friday, 7=Saturday. [] for non-weekly schedules.

monthlyOn.description: Day of month (1-31), use 0 for non-monthly schedules

endDate.description: Only fill when endType is 1 (DATE), otherwise empty string

executedTimes.description: Set to target count when endType is 2 (TIMES), otherwise 0

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier for interpreting the cron time (e.g. 'Asia/Shanghai', 'America/Los_Angeles').
